text:
Brendan Gallagher played 911 games for Montreal, and now, at 34, he's a fourth-line winger on a rebuilding Canucks team, with no goals in 16 games. Our numbers say the drought is mostly bad luck: about three expected goals of chances and nothing to show for it. He keeps going to the net, the way he always has.

The week has been about more than goals. He paid tribute to his former teammate Carey Price ahead of Price's Hall of Fame induction, and Connor Murphy's chirp at him during the Oilers game went viral. Sportsnet wrote about him leaning on his experience to help the Canucks through a rebuild, which is probably the most important thing he does there now.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.6 wins last season, with his team creating more with him on the ice than with 86% of forwards. Vancouver is roughly even with him on this season, a little better than without him. Our range has him at 5 to 13 goals over a full season. Born in Edmonton, junior hockey in Vancouver, a career in Montreal: the first goal as a Canuck is coming.
headline: Gallagher's first Canucks goal is coming
